stories.headline: Man accused of shooting Thornton police officer charged with attempted murder
stories.summary:
Luis Arebalo, 37, has been charged with three counts of first-degree attempted murder, along with four counts of first-degree assault and seven counts of violent crime. The 17th Judicial District Attorney's Office announced the charges in a Friday news release. The charges stem from the shooting of a Thornton police officer and a multiday search for Arebalo.

The shooting occurred around 9:33 p.m. Sunday, Oct. 11, in the 12800 block of Ulster Street. Officers were responding to an unwanted person report. A caller said an acquaintance, Arebalo, had contacted them on social media, made suicidal statements and then appeared outside their door, Deputy Police Chief Keith Evans said at a Tuesday news conference.

While two officers spoke with the caller, they saw Arebalo across the street and tried to speak with him. Evans said Arebalo opened fire and struck one officer in the lower extremities. One officer returned fire and has been placed on paid administrative leave, as is protocol, pending an investigation. Arebalo fled on foot and was considered armed and dangerous.

Arebalo was arrested Tuesday evening after the search. The officer who was shot was recovering at home as of Tuesday. Arebalo is scheduled to appear in Adams County Court at 8:30 a.m. Nov. 6 for a disposition hearing.

stories.headline: Two people injured in Denver shooting near 32nd and Arapahoe
stories.summary:
Denver police are investigating a shooting that left two people injured early Saturday. The shooting happened around 3:15 a.m. near 32nd and Arapahoe streets.

Police said officers initially believed only one person had been wounded. A second person later arrived at a hospital with gunshot wounds, and police said that person took themselves there.

The investigation into what led up to the shooting is ongoing, and police are still searching for suspects. No information about the victims' conditions was immediately released.

Anyone with information is asked to contact Crime Stoppers at 720-913-STOP (7867).

stories.headline: Denver Summit FC's playoff hopes take hit with 3-2 home loss to Angel City
stories.summary:
Denver Summit FC blew a 2-0 lead Saturday night and fell 3-2 to Angel City before a sold-out crowd at Centennial Stadium. The loss dealt a serious blow to the first-year NWSL franchise's playoff hopes. Angel City scored three goals in 11 minutes to close out the first half.

Melissa Kössler scored the fastest goal in franchise history in the second minute, finishing a deflected corner kick from Janine Sonis. Lindsey Heaps made it 2-0 in the 18th minute with a one-timer from the top of the box. Sveindís Jane Jónsdóttir got Angel City on the board in the 32nd minute, and Summit FC failed to equalize in the second half.

Coach Matt Wells said the team has work to do absorbing pressure and regaining momentum, adding that Summit has too often given away leads. Angel City extended its unbeaten streak to eight matches and sits fifth with 46 points.

Summit FC is 10th with 38 points, behind Utah, Portland, North Carolina and Seattle. North Carolina also lost Saturday, which kept Denver from being eliminated.

stories.headline: Courtland Sutton struggles to get involved in slumping Broncos offense
stories.summary:
Courtland Sutton is off to the worst start of his career, and the Broncos' top two receivers, Sutton and Jaylen Waddle, have had little impact this season. Both are on pace for career lows in receptions, receiving yards and touchdowns. Sutton has 13 catches for 123 yards through six games, compared with an average of 25 catches for 361 yards in the first six games of previous seasons.

Waddle has also struggled. Four of his 10 lowest single-game receiving totals have come in his first six games with the Broncos. In Thursday's overtime win over Seattle, Sutton caught two passes for 19 yards.

Quarterback Bo Nix said he does not know where the disconnect is, and that the offense is struggling to find explosive plays. Denver's passing game has largely become checkdowns to running backs and tight ends. Opposing defenses have stayed in two-high safety and shell looks, and Denver has not made them pay.

The struggles do not fall solely on Nix. Sutton has looked a step slower and has had trouble separating against man coverage, though his average separation is the highest since 2023, according to Next Gen Stats.

stories.headline: Svechkov, Schwartz and Hughes form Avalanche's most consistent line early
stories.summary:
Avalanche forward Fedor Svechkov, Jaden Schwartz and rookie T.J. Hughes have formed Colorado's most consistent line to start the season. Svechkov fought Dallas' Radek Faksa in a 3-2 win Tuesday, his first fight in North America, after Faksa hit Schwartz.

Before Friday's game against Pittsburgh, the trio's worst of the short season, the Avalanche had controlled nearly 62 percent of shot attempts and 70 percent of scoring chances in more than 43 minutes with the line on the ice.

Coach Jared Bednar said he likes their play within the structure of the game and that each brings something different. He is taking a new approach this year, trusting younger players more. Svechkov, who has more than 100 NHL games despite being younger than Hughes, has earned a role on the penalty kill.

Bednar called Svechkov a responsible two-way center with skating ability, length and grit. Schwartz said Svechkov takes key faceoffs and protects the puck well. Bednar said defensive play is what earns ice time on his team.

stories.headline: Lawsuit challenges CPW furbearer limit as Amendment 83 heads to ballot
stories.summary:
Safari Club International and the Sportsmen's Alliance Foundation sued Colorado Parks and Wildlife on Oct. 2 over a two-per-day limit on 17 furbearer species. Commissioners narrowly approved the limit July 16. It covers species including mink, badger, red fox, Western spotted skunk, beaver, bobcat, raccoon and coyote.

CPW staff had recommended species-specific limits of four or eight, or a combined limit of 15. They said current harvests are sustainable. The lawsuit argues the commission gave no prior notice of cuts far below either proposal and denied the public a chance to comment, as state law requires.

The suit centers on a 6-5 vote after Commissioner Rebecca Niemiec introduced a survey of 534 Coloradans that she published the day before the meeting. Niemiec acknowledged the sample was smaller than she had hoped and not yet peer-reviewed. She was nominated in June and has not been confirmed by the state Senate.

The Denver Gazette editorial board cites the case in support of Amendment 83, on the Nov. 3 ballot, which it says would guarantee Coloradans' right to hunt and fish.

stories.headline: When could Denver get an Aldi store?
stories.summary:
Colorado's lack of Aldi grocery stores is expected to end soon. In January, Aldi announced plans to bring 50 stores to Colorado over the next few years.

In July, the company submitted concept plans for two locations near Denver, a sign the retailer is moving from announcement toward construction in the metro area.

The expansion would add a discount grocery option for Denver-area shoppers. Exact opening dates and sites were not detailed in the available report.

stories.headline: Denver forecast calls for unseasonably warm, sunny weather through next week
stories.summary:
The Denver weather forecast calls for tranquil conditions through much of the coming week, with unseasonably warm temperatures and generally sunny skies, according to Fox31 Denver. Forecasters said few changes have been made to the outlook.

The weather is expected to stay quiet statewide into early next week. Moisture is then forecast to return to the Western Slope and San Juan Mountains around Wednesday.

Some of that moisture may try to slip east of the Continental Divide, but forecasters have low confidence in the storm track. Most guidance currently takes the system north of Colorado, though forecasters said they will continue to monitor it.

weather.notable: Nearly 9 degrees above the average high for this time of year.

topStory.headline: Fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta Leaves Several Dead and Many Injured, Overwhelming Hospitals
topStory.summary:
A major fire broke out Saturday in a training area at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, killing and injuring an undetermined number of people, Defence Minister David McGuinty said. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said officers were called shortly after 4 p.m. following reports of a fire at the base. Strong winds, with gusts of up to 100 kilometres an hour, spread the flames through the base's fences and into the surrounding rural area, according to the Municipal District of Wainwright.

McGuinty did not confirm a cause or casualty figures, describing the situation as "very, very active and delicate" and saying it would soon become "an active and delicate investigation." He said the RCMP were involved and that he could not recall a comparable incident in recent memory. Global News, citing unnamed military sources, reported that at least seven people were killed and dozens injured when a gas line or gas well was hit during a live-fire training exercise. That account has not been confirmed by officials.

Hospitals in the region faced intense strain. Dr. Warren Thirsk, an emergency physician at the Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton, about 120 miles northwest of the base, told CBC News that health-care facilities near the base had become "completely overwhelmed" and that patients were being brought to hospitals across Edmonton. He called the event "a one in every 15 to 25-year disaster." CBC reported that the hospital declared a code orange, the protocol for a high-casualty incident.

By 11 p.m., the Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire was being held and that property and critical infrastructure were protected. No evacuation order was issued for residents, though people were urged to avoid the area and yield to emergency vehicles. Prime Minister Mark Carney cited a "serious incident creating a major fire" and said his thoughts were with those affected. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith called the fire "significant and tragic" and said it was affecting many military personnel. Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe said his province had sent assistance, and British Columbia Premier David Eby offered "all possible assistance."

CFB Wainwright is one of Canada's busiest military training bases and the main site for the Canadian military's live-fire exercises. It is home to the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, and about 690 military personnel and 300 civilian workers are on site on a typical day. Wainwright Mayor Bruce Pugh said the town's residents are closely tied to the base, with many neighbours serving or former members of the Armed Forces, and he said he believed the event would become the area's largest-ever mass casualty event. Officials said more information on the casualties and the cause would be released in the coming hours and days as the investigation proceeds.
